title: Building Agent Systems That Survive Real-World Data
summary: Demo-ware breaks the moment inputs stop being clean. Notes on the failure modes that actually show up in production agent pipelines, and the guardrails worth building first.

title: Getting Hallucination Under 10% with Citation Grounding
summary: What it actually took to hold a research agent to a sub-10% hallucination rate: retrieval discipline, typed outputs, and refusing to let the model write anything it cannot point at.

title: The $7 Production Stack
summary: A full multi-agent platform — Postgres, Redis, workers, reverse proxy, auto-SSL — running on AWS for the price of a sandwich. What I cut, and what I refused to cut.

title: Shortcut Learning Is a Bias Problem, Not an Accuracy Problem
summary: Average accuracy hides the failure. Why gradient disagreement turned out to be a more honest signal than misclassification for finding hidden groups.

title: Small Models, Narrow Tasks
summary: Small language models get dismissed because they are measured as general-purpose systems. Tuned for one job, the picture changes considerably.
